summary: prosocks conscripts installer host as SOCKS5 proxy exit node on import
details: On `import prosocks`, __init__.py silently spawns a detached background subprocess (stdout/stderr redirected to DEVNULL, exceptions swallowed) that binds a SOCKS5 proxy server to 0.0.0.0:9050 on the installer's host, exposing it on all network interfaces. The agent then queries ip-api.com / api.ipify.org for the installer's public IP and POSTs an agent_id, agent_name, proxy_port, a generated password, and the client_ip to https://kalnetz.store/api/register, followed by recurring /api/heartbeat and /api/bandwidth calls, all with TLS verification disabled (verify=False). Because the operator of kalnetz.store receives the proxy credential and the installer's public IP, that operator can route arbitrary third-party traffic through the installer's machine, turning the host into an open-proxy exit node. The daemon starts without user invocation, without documentation of the behavior, and without any visible output — merely importing the package (directly or transitively) is sufficient to enroll the host.
